claims.text: The 12-month prevalence of major depressive episodes in adolescents increased from 8.7% in 2005 to 11.3% in 2014.
The 12-month prevalence of major depressive episodes in young adults increased from 8.8% in 2005 to 9.6% in 2014.
The increase in major depressive episode prevalence was larger and statistically significant only in the age range of 12 to 20 years.
Prevalence trends of major depressive episodes remained significant after adjustment for substance use disorders and sociodemographic factors.
Overall mental health care contacts did not change over time between 2005 and 2014.
The use of specialty mental health providers increased in adolescents and young adults between 2005 and 2014.
The use of prescription medications increased in adolescents between 2005 and 2014.
Inpatient hospitalizations increased in adolescents between 2005 and 2014.

evidence.description: The 12-month prevalence of MDEs increased from 8.7% in 2005 to 11.3% in 2014 in adolescents (P < .001).
The 12-month prevalence of MDEs increased from 8.8% to 9.6% in young adults (P < .001).
The increase was larger and statistically significant only in the age range of 12 to 20 years.
The trends remained significant after adjustment for substance use disorders and sociodemographic factors.
Mental health care contacts overall did not change over time.
The use of specialty mental health providers increased in adolescents and young adults.
The use of prescription medications and inpatient hospitalizations increased in adolescents.
The use of prescription medications and inpatient hospitalizations increased in adolescents.

methodologies.name: Cross-sectional trend analysis of national survey data
methodologies.description: Analysis of annual cross-sectional population survey data to evaluate 10-year trends in 12-month prevalence of major depressive episodes and mental health service utilization.
datasets: National Surveys on Drug Use and Health (2005-2014)

future_work.text: Renewed efforts are needed to expand service capacity to best meet the mental health care needs of adolescents and young adults.
